status.note: Sourced from the W3C ARIA APG accordion pattern for roles and keyboard, and Base UI's Accordion for API naming consensus. Note that the APG no longer specifies arrow-key navigation between headers, and Base UI has deprecated its `orientation` and `loopFocus` props to match. Uses the EXPERIMENTAL `collection` block, added to find out whether an accordion can be compiled at all.

intent.purpose: Holds which of a set of sections are expanded, and lets a reader open one without losing the list of the others. It exists so that the open set has exactly one home rather than each section holding its own copy.
behaviour: Holds the open set: which of its sections are expanded. The set lives here rather than in each section, so opening one can close another.
Allows any number of sections open at once, including none.

Adds no keyboard behaviour between headers. Every trigger is an ordinary button in the page's Tab order, which is what the ARIA APG now specifies — it removed roving focus from this pattern, and arrow-key navigation between headers is not part of it.
Disabling the accordion disables every item in it; an individual item may also be disabled on its own.
notFor: Tabs. An accordion's sections stack and more than one may be open; tabs show exactly one panel in a fixed area. Choosing accordion for a tabs job produces a list that jumps as it opens.
A single collapsible section. That is a disclosure, and it needs none of this — no set, no shared state, no coordination.
Navigation. These sections reveal content in place; nothing here changes a URL.
Hiding content from the page's search. A closed panel that is removed from the DOM cannot be found by the browser's find-in-page, which is a real cost and the reason a keep-mounted option exists.

orientation.description: Only vertical is designed. Recorded as an axis with one value rather than omitted, because the horizontal case exists in the canon and this component deliberately does not take it.

disabled.description: The whole accordion ignores interaction. Cascades to every item.
disabled.visual: Every header dims and no panel can be toggled.

a11y.keyboard: Tab and Shift+Tab move between triggers as ordinary buttons. Enter and Space toggle the focused section. No arrow-key navigation — the APG does not specify it for this pattern.
notes: Each header must be wrapped in a heading element whose level fits the surrounding page, and the trigger button must be the only thing inside that heading. This component cannot know what heading level is correct for a page it does not own, so the level must be passed in and there is no safe default.

In single mode the open section's trigger is marked disabled for assistive technology, because activating it would do nothing. That is the APG's guidance and it means a keyboard user can still focus it and be told why it will not respond.
A panel removed from the DOM when closed is invisible to find-in-page. Keeping it mounted fixes that and costs rendering every panel's content whether or not anyone opens it.
The accordion has no accessible name of its own and does not need one — each section is named by its own heading.

children.description: The sections, in order. Anything else is passed through untouched but takes no part in the open set.

root.description: The wrapper holding the sections, so they stack as one unit and can be given a shared border treatment.
